catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural, domain, and behavioral patterns extracted from the cas_runner codebase, excluding LLM prompt flows and agent orchestration.
analysis_limits: Analysis conducted strictly on provided repository manifest, directory tree, and module symbols.
Implementation details inferred from class definitions, symbol names, and documentation artifacts.

system_map.overview: Layered continuous architecture and operational governance runtime that parses git deltas, evaluates compliance rules, models capability sets, and drives governance actions across repository lifecycles.

layers.name: Presentation / CLI Layer
layers.purpose: Command-line interface entry points for invoking runner flows and bootstrap procedures.

layers.name: Application & Orchestration Layer
layers.purpose: Coordinates governance workflows, state transitions, workspace bootstrap, and dashboard projections.

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.purpose: Core business models, typed governance abstractions, health indicators, and transition logic.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Storage Layer
layers.purpose: File-system layout storage for knowledge templates, git change capture, and pluggable client adapters.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Core governance entities and architectural concepts are modeled as strongly-typed Pydantic classes with explicit serialization and validation rules.
patterns.intent: Ensure robust data integrity, schema enforcement, and seamless serialization across system boundaries without relying on unstructured dictionaries.
patterns.context: The system processes compliance findings, governance health scores, steering capability records, and git deltas that must be serialized to JSON/YAML or passed between domain services.
forces: Need for runtime type checking and validation of input configurations
Requirement to serialize domain models into knowledge store markdown/YAML files
Desire to avoid loose dictionary structures prone to KeyError exceptions
patterns.solution: Define data transfer objects and domain models using Pydantic models (e.g. `GovernanceInventory`, `ComplianceFinding`, `CapabilityRecord`, `ArchitecturalDelta`) to enforce strict types and default initializers.
implementation_signals: Model classes defined in models.py files
Typed attributes with default values and validation constraints

evidence.note: Defines domain structures for governance evaluation, risks, actions, and findings.
Defines architectural capability sets and steering index records.

benefits: Eliminates parsing ambiguity across CLI and workflow boundaries
Automatic schema validation during deserialization from disk
costs: Runtime validation overhead on object instantiation
Dependency on Pydantic v2 data model structures
failure_modes: ValidationError exceptions when disk templates or files contain schema drift

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: State transitions for governance actions and architectural lifecycles are registered in an explicit transition registry decoupled from execution.
patterns.intent: Maintain deterministic and auditable state transitions for governance tasks while allowing extensible registration of new state changes.
patterns.context: Governance tasks move through distinct lifecycle phases (e.g., detected, evaluated, resolved, exempted) that require explicit transition gates.
forces: Need to prevent illegal state changes across long-running governance lifecycles
Extensibility for adding custom domain transitions without altering the core engine
patterns.solution: Encapsulate lifecycle states and valid transitions in a `TransitionRegistry` managed by `GovernanceActionEngine`.
implementation_signals: Separation of transition validation from action execution logic

evidence.note: TransitionRegistry manages valid state mutations and actions executed by GovernanceActionEngine.

benefits: Explicit catalog of valid governance lifecycle transitions
Centralized audit point for state transition rules
costs: Requires state transitions to be declared prior to execution
failure_modes: Unregistered transitions cause workflow halts or unhandled domain exceptions

patterns.name: Service Facade and Engine Separation
patterns.summary: Application services coordinate business flows by delegating computational and rule verification logic to dedicated domain engines.
patterns.intent: Isolate high-level orchestration, coordination, and IO from deterministic domain rule evaluation and action engines.
patterns.context: Execution requires evaluating compliance rules and applying governance actions against current workspace models.
forces: Separation of concerns between orchestration logic and rule evaluation
Enables unit testing domain engines independently of outer service workflows
patterns.solution: Expose `GovernanceActionService` as an application layer entry point that orchestrates `GovernanceActionEngine` and `ComplianceEngine` instances.
implementation_signals: Coexistence of Service classes and Engine classes in the same module namespace
Service layer delegating computational calls to engine classes

evidence.note: Coordinates operations by delegating domain mutations to engine instances.

benefits: Clean separation between transaction orchestration and domain rule validation
Easier mocking and isolation in unit tests
costs: Extra layer of indirection between caller and domain engines
failure_modes: Service becoming a pass-through layer if domain engine boundaries are not maintained

patterns.name: Declarative File-System Knowledge Repository
patterns.summary: System architectural knowledge, rules, decisions, and signals are persisted declaratively as structured files within a standardized folder hierarchy.
patterns.intent: Enable human-readable, version-controlled architecture governance artifacts alongside code without mandatory database infrastructure.
patterns.context: Architecture continuous governance relies on ADRs, patterns, rules, and runtime profiles that must be inspectable and auditable in Git.
forces: Need for version-controlled knowledge persistence using standard Git workflows
Ease of templating and manual developer contributions
patterns.solution: Establish a standardized folder tree (`cas-knowledge/global/`, `cas-knowledge/projects/`, `cas-knowledge/runtime/`, `cas-knowledge/templates/`) containing markdown, yaml, and json files with corresponding bootstrap scaffolding.
implementation_signals: Dedicated cas-knowledge directory tree with subdirectories for decisions, rules, and patterns
Template markdown files in templates/ directory
Bootstrap utilities to initialize and merge workspace blocks

evidence.note: Standardized templates for persisting architecture knowledge on disk.
Utilities ensuring file structures and governance blocks are scaffolded.

benefits: Zero external database dependency; native Git auditability and PR reviews
Easily processed by static site generators (MkDocs)
costs: File system I/O latency and potential concurrent write collisions
Risk of manual file corruption bypassing programmatic validators
failure_modes: Directory layout drift or missing required template keys when modified directly on disk

patterns.name: Pluggable Provider Adapter
patterns.summary: External integration points are abstracted behind common interfaces with concrete live and mock implementations.
patterns.intent: Decouple domain business logic from remote network clients, allowing offline execution, deterministic testing, and interchangeable backends.
patterns.context: The platform requires client integrations (e.g., LiteLLM) that may fail in offline or CI environments.
forces: Need for reliable unit and integration testing without network calls or API keys
Interchangeability of concrete underlying client implementations
patterns.solution: Provide parallel client implementations (such as LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient) that conform to the expected client interface.
implementation_signals: Paired client classes like LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient in the client module
Conditional instantiation based on execution profile or environment

evidence.note: Test double providing predictable mock responses without external calls.

benefits: Allows testing workflows in air-gapped or CI environments
Isolates external dependency upgrades from domain logic
costs: Maintenance burden of keeping mock implementations in sync with live adapters
failure_modes: Mock client behavior diverging from production client behavior

patterns.name: Pure Functional Health Evaluation
patterns.summary: Health metrics calculation is separated into side-effect-free pure functions that map domain inventory and finding states to health enumerations.
patterns.intent: Ensure deterministic, testable, and transparent health status derivation without mutable state or hidden side effects.
patterns.context: The governance dashboard requires real-time health assessment and diagnostic reasons derived from current project governance inventories.
forces: Need for clear traceability between underlying compliance findings and top-level health indicators
Avoidance of mutable calculation states in dashboard rendering
patterns.solution: Implement stateless calculation functions (`calculate_health`, `get_health_reasons`) that accept domain inputs and return typed `HealthStatus` enumerations and explanation strings.
implementation_signals: Stateless functions named calculate_* in dashboard/health_model.py

evidence.note: Functional evaluation of health states and human-readable diagnostic reasons.

benefits: High testability with predictable outputs given specific inputs
No risk of race conditions or state pollution between evaluations
costs: Requires caller to assemble and pass full domain state snapshots
failure_modes: Incomplete input snapshots yielding false healthy statuses

patterns.name: Delta-Based Change Modeling
patterns.summary: Repository mutations are ingested and represented as explicit discrete delta models rather than diffing snapshots continuously.
patterns.intent: Provide a first-class domain representation of code and architecture changes to trigger precise steering and governance checks.
patterns.context: Continuous governance needs to inspect pull requests and git commits to determine which architectural capabilities are affected.
forces: Diff operations are raw text and lack domain context
Downstream governance engines need structured representations of changes
patterns.solution: Model changes using `RawGitDelta`, `GitChangeType`, and `ArchitecturalDelta` entities that capture paths, change types, and architectural impact metadata.

evidence.note: Encapsulates repository mutations into structured domain entities.

benefits: Standardizes change analysis across different VCS sources
Enables filtering and targeted rule execution based on affected file types
costs: Requires pre-processing step to convert git diffs into typed delta models
failure_modes: Inaccurate parsing of complex git diffs or file renames resulting in malformed deltas

anti_patterns.name: Coupling Domain Services to Concrete File Paths
symptoms: Hardcoded relative folder paths across multiple modules (e.g. cas-knowledge/global/...)
Direct disk access dispersed across services rather than behind a repository interface
impact: Difficulty executing tests in temporary or in-memory file systems
Fragility when altering the workspace folder structure
suggested_remediation: Introduce an AbstractKnowledgeStore interface that abstracts file system operations behind get/put methods.
Pass configured workspace roots via dependency injection to services.

anti_patterns.name: Anemic Domain Models with Dispersed Engine Logic
symptoms: Domain models primarily behave as passive data bags (Pydantic models with only field definitions)
Business operations and state validation residing strictly in external Engine classes
impact: Risk of creating invalid entity states when instantiated outside engine workflows
Duplication of domain logic across different services
suggested_remediation: Encapsulate invariants and core validation logic directly within the domain entity classes using Pydantic model validators.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Observability & Telemetry
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Dependencies on opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk provide distributed tracing and metric collection across workflow executions.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Documentation as Artifacts
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integration with MkDocs, mkdocs-material, and drawio plugins to compile knowledge repository markdown artifacts into interactive documentation portals.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent filesystem writes coordinated when multiple actions execute in parallel?
open_questions.context: The repository uses local file-based storage under cas-knowledge without visible file locking primitives.
